replies.author: @AmazingGlobalDiscoveries
replies.text: Nowruz has very ancient roots and is celebrated by many different peoples and cultures today, including Iranians, Turkic communities, Kurds, Central Asians, and others. In the video, we were referring to its long history in the Iranian cultural sphere, not trying to deny anyone else’s connection to the holiday.

replies.author: @AmazingGlobalDiscoveries
replies.text: Yeah! Iran is indeed home to a very large Turkic-speaking population, especially Iranian Azerbaijanis, as well as many other ethnic groups such as Persians, Kurds, Lurs, Arabs, Baluch and others. Iran’s diversity is one of the most fascinating parts of its culture.

comments.author: @RealLifeFilesDoc
comments.text: Western media always paints Iran as a barren desert filled with restrictions. The truth? They have a 50-million-year-old rainforest (Hercanian), 30 alpine ski resorts, and women make up the MAJORITY of university students (with one of the highest rates of female engineers in the world)! Never confuse the people with the politics of their government. What surprised you the most about Iran after watching this? 🇮🇷✨
